title: Cocoa butter and vanilla cold-process soap
subtitle: A rich, hard bar with a warm, sweet scent
excerpt: A cold-process bar made with a generous proportion of cocoa butter alongside olive and coconut oils, scented with vanilla fragrance oil. The cocoa butter hardens the bar, adds a faint chocolatey undertone, and gives the lather a silky texture. Makes seven bars; cure four to six weeks.
sourceNotes: Cocoa butter in cold-process soap: Susan Miller Cavitch, The Soapmaker's Companion (1997). Cocoa butter SAP value: 0.137. Vanilla fragrance oil discoloration: vanilla accelerates to trace and darkens the batter to brown during cure, normal, not a defect. SAP values: olive oil 0.134, coconut oil 0.190, castor oil 0.128. 5% superfat. Water 33% of oil weight.

recipe.batchNotes: Run any weight change through a lye calculator. Vanilla fragrance oil can cause batter to seize or accelerate quickly, have the mould ready before you blend.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bar darkens significantly during cure due to the vanilla; a fully cured bar is deep chocolate-brown on the outside. The vanilla scent fades slightly but stabilises.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years or more in a cool dark cupboard. The cocoa butter and high coconut content make this a long-lasting bar. Discard if DOS or a sharp paint-like smell appears.

glossaryTerms.definition: The point at which soap batter thickens so that a drizzle on the surface briefly holds its shape. Vanilla fragrance oil is known to accelerate trace, have the mould positioned and ready when blending starts.

The chemical reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide that produces soap and glycerine. Cocoa butter participates in saponification like any fat; its hardness-contributing fatty acids remain in the finished bar's structure.

projectSchedule.title: Unmould and cut
projectSchedule.body: Turn out the loaf after 48 hours wearing gloves. The bar will already be noticeably dark, vanilla darkens the batter to caramel-brown during the first day. Cut into bars and set on a rack.

projectSchedule.title: Six-week cure complete
projectSchedule.body: The fully cured bar is deep chocolate-brown on the outside, often with a lighter interior if the gel phase was partial. Hard and firm to the touch. The vanilla scent is warm and faint, it stabilises after the first few weeks of cure.

content.text: Cocoa butter and vanilla soap is a cold-process bar made with cocoa butter, olive, coconut, and castor oils, scented with vanilla fragrance oil. The cocoa butter hardens the bar and adds a faint chocolatey note; vanilla fragrance oil gives it a warm, sweet smell that deepens during the cure. Makes seven bars; cure four to six weeks
. The process is called
saponification
Wear protective gloves and goggles before handling lye. Vanilla fragrance oil can cause the batter to thicken quickly at
trace
, have the mould ready before you start blending.
Ingredients

items.prepNote: 30% of oil weight; melt gently; provides hardness and lather
20% of oil weight; melt with the coconut oil
NaOH at 99% purity; calculated for 5% superfat on this oil blend
3% of oil weight; added at light trace; add quickly and pour immediately

content.text: Method
Mix the lye solution

In a ventilated space, wearing gloves and goggles, pour the distilled water into the HDPE pitcher. Add the sodium hydroxide in a steady stream while stirring. Never add water to lye. Set aside to cool to 38 to 42°C.
Melt and prepare the oils
Melt the cocoa butter and coconut oil together over a low heat. Combine with olive and castor oils in a heatproof bowl. Cool to 38 to 42°C.
Blend to trace and add fragrance

Pour the lye solution into the oils in a thin stream, stirring as you go. Stick-blend to a light trace only. Add the vanilla fragrance oil and stir by hand for a few seconds. Pour into the mould immediately, do not stick-blend after the vanilla is added.
Pour, insulate, unmould, cure

Pour into the silicone loaf mould and smooth the top quickly. Wrap in a towel to insulate for 24 hours. Unwrap and leave for another 24 hours. Turn out wearing gloves, cut into bars, and cure on a rack for four to six weeks.
Colour note

Vanilla fragrance oil turns the soap dark during cure. A fully cured bar is deep chocolate-brown on the outside. Vanillin in the fragrance oil reacts with the soap and produces the colour; it does not affect performance.
Storage and shelf life
Store in a cool, dark cupboard for two years or more. Discard if orange rancid patches or a sharp paint-like smell develops.
